title: Knowledge Check 8: Lessons 36-39
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 36-39 of the ai-adoption series. Score 80% or higher to progress toward the practice exam.

questions.question: Lesson 36 sorts market signals into classes that always authorize action and classes that need a threshold. Which of the following does it put in the always-act group?
options: A vendor retiring the model that one of your workflows runs on
A competitor's press release announcing an agentic claims product
A newer model taking the top spot on a public leaderboard
A trade-press rumor that one of your vendors may be acquired
questions.explanation: Lesson 36 names three always-act classes: lifecycle notices, terms and data changes, and regulatory or contractual deadlines. A retirement announcement has a date the vendor set, so there is nothing to debate. The other three options are capability or market claims, which carry thresholds and are logged with a revisit date rather than acted on immediately.

questions.question: The lesson tells you to build a twenty to thirty task evaluation set from your own workflow rather than tracking published benchmark scores. What reason does it give?
options: Public benchmarks are behind paywalls and the scores are not publicly released
A thirty task set produces statistically rigorous rankings between close models
Regulators require organizations to maintain an internal evaluation set

Public benchmarks have begun to saturate, so ranking the leaders by published scores says little about your work, while your own set measures the change on your tasks and catches a regression when a vendor updates a model behind a moving alias
questions.explanation: Lesson 36 cites the 2026 AI Index finding that evaluations are being outpaced by the progress they measure and that the gap between top models is shrinking, plus the MMLU-Pro result that prompt style alone moved scores by 4 to 5 percent. It also states plainly that thirty tasks is a smoke detector, not statistics, and is not enough to rank two close models.

questions.question: In the worked example, four pieces of market news reach Owen in one quarter. Which one moved the roadmap, and why?
options: The retirement notice, because every deprecation forces an immediate switch of the affected workflow
The price cut, because it crossed a threshold Owen set in advance and made a previously rejected extension clear its business case at the new unit cost, inside the team's remaining change capacity
The competitor announcement, because a competitive threat overrides the annual plan
The newer model, because a better published benchmark score is the standard trigger for switching
questions.explanation: Lesson 36 has Owen log the retirement with a migration scheduled into an existing third-quarter change slot rather than a roadmap change, log the capability release and the competitor claim with revisit dates, and act only on the price cut, which passed the 25 percent line written into the watch log in January and cleared the extension's business case within underwriting's remaining capacity.

questions.question: Lesson 37 draws a line between a health review and a steering committee. Which statement matches the distinction the lesson makes?
options: A steering committee decides whether to fund something. A health review decides whether the thing you already funded is still healthy, still used, still compliant, and still worth its cost.
A steering committee meets quarterly and a health review meets annually, and both approve new spending at the end of the cycle
A health review is the external audit that produces formal findings for the board, while a steering committee receives them
A steering committee reads the data pack and the health review compiles it, so the two meetings should never share an attendee list
questions.explanation: The lesson states that a steering committee decides whether to fund something, while a health review decides whether what you already funded is still healthy, still used, still compliant, and still worth its cost. It warns that merging the two agendas is how funding decisions crowd out looking after what you already own. Same people, different question, different agenda.

questions.question: A deferral keeps reappearing in the ledger because nobody ever puts a date on the next decision. Which line from the lesson covers that situation?
options: A missing number has an address rather than an apology
One loud item cannot eat the whole meeting
A deferral with no new date is a deletion
Deferrals should be cleared by the chair before the pack is circulated
questions.explanation: In the deferral ledger block of the agenda, the lesson says every item whose revisit date has arrived gets a decision, even if the decision is to defer again with a new date and a stated reason, and then states that a deferral with no new date is a deletion. The other options come from the data pack rules and the time boxes, not from the ledger block.

questions.question: In the worked example, two near misses happen because adjusters pasted policy schedules into a public chatbot. What does the review do about them?
options: It records a training failure and schedules a reminder email for every adjuster in the pilot
It is a content gap with a training failure on top, and the fix is to load the schedules, not to send a reminder email.
It escalates the incident to the regulator and freezes claims document intake for two weeks
It revokes the adjusters' access to the assistant platform until retraining is complete
questions.explanation: The review refuses to treat the near misses as a training failure, because both have the same shape and the cause is that the approved tool did not have the document the adjusters needed. The lesson calls it a content gap with a training failure on top and points the fix at loading the policy schedules. It then requires the sampling to be re-run after the schedules are loaded.

questions.question: Nadia's team wrote scale gates before they needed them, and three existing pilots failed the first line. Why did killing two of them not cost her political capital?
options: Because the killed pilots were run by contractors rather than by employees, so no internal team lost work
The teams involved were not told no. They were told not yet, with a date.
Because the scale gate applied only to new use cases, so pilots already running were left alone
Because the executive sponsor announced the cancellations in writing and absorbed the criticism
questions.explanation: The lesson says the team prepared a one-page note for each killed pilot explaining what it was, what it would have needed, and the date it would be reconsidered, and that this note is the reason the cancellations did not cost political capital. The teams were given a date rather than a refusal. The lesson adds that a pilot without a decision date is a small permanent deployment with no review.

questions.question: The lesson says Nadia converted change capacity into a number. What did she actually do to get that number?
options: She benchmarked her operations teams against change-capacity averages her vendors published
She set a company-wide ceiling of eleven process changes and applied it equally to every team
She asked each team lead how many process changes their team could absorb and wrote the numbers down in a single list
Nadia asked each of the six operations directors one question: how many process changes can your team absorb this quarter without service levels slipping?
questions.explanation: The answers ranged from one to three and totaled eleven, and the lesson says eleven became the budget, with a twelfth idea going into a queue with a date rather than into a meeting with enthusiasm. It also calls this the single most transferable move in the lesson and the one that requires the most nerve. Saying the number out loud means refusing work that a senior person just proposed.

questions.question: Which measurement does Lesson 38 call the least glamorous metric in the course and the one that most reliably finds real money?
options: Licence utilisation is the least glamorous metric in this course and the one that most reliably finds real money.
Weekly active use measured across the whole estate
Cost per automated customs entry against the manual alternative
Open findings from the internal review that are dated and owned
questions.explanation: In the month eighteen section the lesson notes that of 780 licensed seats, 620 are genuinely used weekly and 160 are not, and that the team reviews that gap every quarter rather than celebrating the higher seat count. It then states plainly that licence utilisation is the least glamorous metric in the course and the one that most reliably finds real money. The try-it section turns that into an exercise: multiply the unused seats by the annual unit price.

questions.question: Air Canada argued it could not be held liable for what its website chatbot told a passenger about bereavement fares. What did the tribunal decide?
options: That the airline was liable only for its static webpages, because the chatbot ran on a third-party product
That the passenger should have checked the separate bereavement travel webpage, so the claim failed
It makes no difference whether the information comes from a static page or a chatbot
That the chatbot was a separate legal entity responsible for its own statements
questions.explanation: Lesson 39 describes the airline's argument as the instinct that a machine's statement is not the company's problem, and reports that the tribunal rejected it, calling the submission that the chatbot was a separate legal entity a remarkable one. The decision holds that it makes no difference whether the information comes from a static page or a chatbot. The order was only $812.02, which the lesson calls a tiny amount and an enormous precedent.

questions.question: The lesson draws a rule from the marketing claim the quality team could not demonstrate. Which line states that rule?
options: Claims about capability are testable, and the test is whether you can produce the evidence.
Capability claims only need review once a regulator asks for supporting documents
Marketing claims sit outside AI governance, which covers operational systems only
A claim is acceptable if the vendor's own documentation supports it, whether or not your team can
questions.explanation: Failure four describes a published claim that the company uses machine learning to guarantee allergen-safe substitutions in every order, which the quality team could not demonstrate. The lesson ties that to the SEC's settled charges against two investment advisers for false and misleading statements about their use of AI and the instruction that if you claim to use AI you must ensure your representations are not false or misleading. It then states that claims about capability are testable, and the test is whether you can produce the evidence.

questions.question: When the supplier cost schedule was pasted into a public assistant, Dana's team could not answer whether it had to be reported, and it took eleven days to work out. What does the lesson say that delay reveals?
options: That the manager who pasted the schedule had ignored a written prohibition
Eleven days is not a disclosure path. It is a policy absence with a calendar attached.
That the tool should have blocked the paste automatically, as vendor contracts require
That the disclosure was not reportable, so no defined path was actually needed
questions.explanation: Failure five describes an incident path that did not exist, so nobody could answer in under a minute who needed to know or whether an external obligation applied. The lesson calls the eleven days not a disclosure path but a policy absence with a calendar attached. It also notes that the generative AI profile treats incident disclosure as one of only four primary considerations.
